title: One letter changes the whole hash

yt.title: I changed ONE letter. {bits} of 256 bits flipped #Shorts
yt.description:
We computed SHA-256 for the words "{word_a}" and "{word_b}" and compared them bit by bit. Everything shown is calculated by code, not drawn.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: I changed one letter. Look at what happened to the fingerprint.
A hash turns any text into a fixed fingerprint, sixty four characters long.

scenes.label: Bits that flipped out of 256
scenes.narration: One letter flipped {bits} of the two hundred fifty six bits. About half.
Every red square is a bit that changed. There is no pattern to follow.

scenes.text: Why passwords are stored this way
scenes.narration: That is why websites should store a fingerprint like this, not your password. So, what happens if I change one more letter?
